title: Quartz Solar AI Cloudcasting - predicting cloud movements through satellite imagery
summary: Open Climate Fix reports that predicted satellite images from its Cloudcasting model raised the accuracy of its PVNet solar forecasts by 5% at two hours ahead.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Cloudcasting began as a 2024 Manchester Prize entry by Open Climate Fix with the Alan Turing Institute. As a finalist, the project received £100,000 in the prize, which the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology runs. On 20 February 2025, Open Climate Fix published an early evaluation of the model. It reported that Cloudcasting input gave a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour horizon when integrated into PVNet, its solar forecasting model. It also reported that cloud forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) added 2.5% when integrated into PVNet. Open Climate Fix planned to add Cloudcasting to Quartz Solar in the United Kingdom by summer 2025. Its release of 6 November 2025 on the adoption of Quartz Solar in the control room of the National Energy System Operator does not mention Cloudcasting. The developer's code repository describes the model as running live in production, and the repository received updates in August 2026. No source reports a measured effect of Cloudcasting in live forecasts. The annual carbon savings remain projected.
purpose: Improve short-horizon solar forecasts through predicted satellite imagery.

ratings.reason: Open Climate Fix reports a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour horizon in its own test on past data, and no source reports that live forecasts improved after Cloudcasting went into production.
The annual saving of 100,000 tons of emissions is a projection, and no source reports that the saving occurred.

ai_role.statement: Open Climate Fix compares its PVNet solar model with and without the predicted satellite images from Cloudcasting and reports that the Cloudcasting input adds 5% accuracy at two hours ahead, against 2.5% from ECMWF cloud forecasts. The developer ran the comparison itself and gives no test period or error measure, and no independent party has repeated it.
